1.1.0.en: Moved microphone audio date from UDP to API. Fixed issue with Agent timing. Switched transcription model. Set interrupt_response to false.

1.1.2.en: Fixed so agent better understands user input and it's own instrunctions

1.1.4.en: Agent should understand even better now, and be less critical to user input. Also other bugfixes.

1.2.0.en: Adds weather answers and awareness of your local time and location. Faster, smoother conversations with better speech understanding. Supports the latest Voice PE firmware, and fixes device pairing so devices show up reliably when you add them.

1.3.0.en: Set timers and alarms with your voice — just say "set a 10 minute timer" or "wake me at 7". The device counts down on its LED ring and chimes when time's up, and you can cancel it by voice. New Flow cards let you start, cancel, and react to timers in your automations, and the device tile now shows the active timer's name and time remaining.

1.4.0.en: Choose your voice engine: Google Gemini is now supported alongside OpenAI, each with its own selectable voices. The assistant now speaks many more languages — pick yours in Settings. Follow-up questions feel more natural in back-and-forth conversations, and asking for the current time or date is now reliable.

1.4.1.en: New device: ThirdReality Voice & Music Assistant. New voice engines: Mistral, plus a fully local pipeline (Whisper, Ollama, Piper and more) that keeps your voice in your home. Set up a new device's Wi-Fi over Bluetooth right from pairing. The assistant can now play music (Music Assistant), manage your Bring! shopping list, and search the web. Redesigned settings page and many stability fixes.

1.4.2.en: You can now add a device by entering its IP address manually if it isn't found automatically during pairing.

1.4.3.en: Devices with API encryption enabled (the default once adopted by Home Assistant) now work — enter the device's encryption key during pairing or in the device settings, and the connection is fully encrypted. Encrypted devices are detected automatically when you add them.

1.4.4.en: Conversations flow much better: a short chime now tells you when the assistant is ready for your follow-up, the microphone reopens about two seconds faster, and conversations no longer end before you get a chance to answer. Fixes non-English voices speaking with an English accent. Unlocking locks by voice is now off by default — enable 'Allow unlocking by voice' in the app settings if you want it.

1.4.5.en: Important fix: in rare cases the assistant could "hear" a command nobody said during a silent pause and act on it — that can no longer happen. Listening now ends after 10 seconds of silence with a soft descending chime so you know the microphone has closed. New experimental device: Seeed ReSpeaker XVF3800. New advanced settings: per-device microphone gain and speech-detection tuning. The Gemini engine now shows the listening LED correctly.

1.4.6.en: Fix: after a brief internet outage, the 'Ask assistant. Output as text' flow card could keep failing until the app was restarted — the assistant now recovers fully on its own once the connection returns. Voice conversations were unaffected. Also removes a stray 'null' that was appended to some error log lines.

1.4.7.en: Fix: Seeed ReSpeaker XVF3800 devices could not be picked in Flow cards — 'Say', 'Ask assistant', 'Playback audio from URL', the timer cards and the assistant triggers now all offer them, just like the other voice devices. Also gives the ReSpeaker a clearer device icon.

1.4.8.en: New experimental device: M5Stack AtomS3R with Atomic Echo Base, running M5Stack's official ESPHome voice-assistant firmware. Pair it via the network scan (paste the API encryption key if it was previously set up with Home Assistant) or by entering its IP address.

1.4.9.en: Web search now checks its own answer and searches again when it comes back vague, and says "let me look that up" while it works. Fixes: a wake word followed by silence could leave the device deaf until it reconnected; the Voice PE now receives the transcript and real error details from the app; and an M5Stack AtomS3R you renamed in ESPHome no longer fails to pair — add it by entering its IP address.

1.4.10.en: The on/off switch on the device tile is now called "Start conversation", because that is what it does: switch it on and the device chimes and listens, so you can speak without saying the wake word. Switching it off now cancels a conversation that is running — useful if the device is stuck listening. In the custom pipeline you can now set the language model or the speech output to "None": with no language model the device just sends you what it heard, for your own Flows to answer; with no speech output the answer comes back as text so a Flow can speak it on another speaker.

1.4.11.en: New: the assistant's spoken reply can be handed to a Flow as an audio link instead of playing on the device — pick "Send to a Flow as a URL" under Reply audio in the device settings and use the new "Reply audio is ready" trigger to play it on a Sonos or any other speaker. Useful for devices without a speaker of their own. The settings page also gains a Debug section: a list of every voice device seen on your network (so you can tell a pairing problem from a network problem) and an optional "What did I just say?" recorder that plays back what the microphone actually captured, so you can tell a microphone problem from a speech-recognition one. Fix: replies could intermittently fail to play, with the device retrying the same audio over and over, because the app told it an address it could not reach.

1.4.12.en: Replies sent to a Flow as an audio link are now MP3 instead of FLAC, so they play on far more speakers — a Sonos in particular. The app's own sounds now come through the same trigger: a short cue when the device starts listening, plus the error, missing-key and post-pairing sounds, which devices without their own speaker could not play before. A new "Is a sound effect" tag lets a Flow tell those apart from a spoken reply. Fix: the audio link could point at an address your speaker was unable to reach, so nothing played. Fix: on newer ESPHome firmware the volume and mute controls, and playing music on the device, could stop working.

1.5.0.en: New: the Custom pipeline can now run on Anthropic's Claude, with the model picked from a live list, and the cloud services for its speech and text stages — OpenAI, Groq, OpenRouter, DeepSeek — are now a dropdown that fills in the address and a working model for you. The pipeline settings are reorganised into one card per stage, and speech-to-text can be given hints (a context sentence and expected words) so short commands and names come back right. Important fix: adding a device could reboot your voice satellite on some ESPHome firmware versions, which showed up as pairing timing out or a device stuck Unavailable. An unavailable device now says which side is down — the device or the voice engine — and the Debug page shows the two separately, alongside a new Verbose logging switch for when you need to send in a log. Setting up Wi-Fi over Bluetooth now notices straight away if the device drops the link. Fixes a crash when a device was deleted, and the Home Assistant Voice PE now trims the wake word from the start of a command by default.

1.5.2.en: New Dump log button under Settings, Debug: writes the app's recent log, including the detailed satellite and voice-engine lines, to a file on your Homey and shows a link you can open on your phone or computer and attach to a forum post or e-mail. API keys, your spoken commands and the assistant's replies are removed before the file is written, and it is deleted again after 30 minutes. Fix: quiet but clear speech on the ThirdReality satellite could end the turn with "Heard nothing" after 8 seconds; the voice detector now picks up softer speech and, when in doubt, sends what it heard to speech recognition instead of giving up.

1.5.3.en: New: blinds, curtains and awnings can now be controlled by voice — open, close, stop or set a position ("open the sunshade halfway"). New: when the room you are in has none of the device you asked for, and exactly one other room does, the assistant acts there and tells you which room (switch under Settings, Smart home control). Faster wake cue when replies are sent to a Flow as a URL: the sound clips are prepared at startup instead of on the first wake. Fix: with the Gemini engine, a short command could be written down in the wrong language (Dutch heard as German) even though the spoken reply was right. Fix: tools could answer from a slightly outdated list of devices. Fix: a satellite whose speaker never starts playing (seen on the M5Stack AtomS3R) no longer leaves the assistant stuck with the ring lit; the turn now ends by itself after a few seconds.

1.5.4.en: Fix: if your OpenAI project is not allowed to use one of the models the app needs (a setting on OpenAI's dashboard), the app now falls back to another model and sends you a notification telling you which model to allow, instead of silently never answering. Speech recognition falls back from gpt-4o-transcribe to gpt-4o-mini-transcribe or whisper-1, and the Say card falls back from gpt-4o-mini-tts to tts-1; the turn that hit the problem is still answered from the audio itself.

1.5.5.en: Fix: the assistant now always reads the current state of your devices when you speak to it. Previously, a light switched on or off some other way (a wall switch, the Homey app, a Flow) could still look unchanged to the assistant, so it would refuse to turn it back on or off, saying it already was. New: if a voice device is still added to Home Assistant, Home Assistant can take over its voice assistant, so the device keeps answering you but Homey never hears you. The app now detects this and tells you: a warning on the device, a notification in your Homey timeline, and a spoken message on the device itself. Remove the device from Home Assistant to fix it.
